newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan holds county by-election after Nov shooting.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan holds county by-election after Nov shooting.

text.p: People in a northern Taiwan county cast their ballots on Saturday, four months after the county's magistrate and seven others were shot dead in one of the island's most sensational crimes in recent memory.
The Taoyuan County by-election was hotly contested by candidates from the ruling Nationalist Party, the pro-independence Democratic Progressive Party and the fledgling New Party.
The final result was expected around 8.00 p.m. (1200 GMT).
In November, two gunmen burst into magistrate Liu Pang-yu's home, bound the hands of Liu and eight others and systematically shot each in the head at close range.
Five died at the scene. Liu, 54, a member of the ruling Nationalist Party, and two others died at hospital.
The public has expressed fears over the social chaos that has accompanied Taiwan's decade-old democratic renaissance, and concerns over some politicians' close ties to organised crime.
The new magistrate will only serve until the end of this year, when Taiwan will hold elections for all cities and counties on the island.
